paragraphs: Friend, here's the lesson that sits right in the middle of this passage. The people ASKED for God's answer, and they promised to obey it, pleasant or unpleasant (Jeremiah 42:5-6). Then the answer came, they didn't like it, and they called Jeremiah a liar. Asking God for direction is one thing. Actually wanting His answer is another, and this passage shows us the gap between the two.

Now look at where they ended up. They went to Egypt to get away from the king of Babylon, and the LORD said He would send for that very king, His servant Nebuchadnezzar, and set his throne over stones buried at Pharaoh's palace (Jeremiah 43:10). The place they picked to feel safe is the place the LORD named. I've watched myself dodge a hard thing, friend, and I'm telling you, running in the opposite direction never got me out of it. Disobedience doesn't take you out of reach of what you feared. It just moves you away from the One who told you the truth.

But hear this part too. The LORD didn't walk away from this crowd. Right there in Tahpanhes, in the middle of their disobedience, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah again (Jeremiah 43:8). So when God asks you to do something hard, baker, let your yes be a real yes, before the answer comes. And if you've already taken a wrong turn, the LORD is still speaking, so keep your ears open. This story isn't over, and neither is what the LORD has to say.
